parameterNotes.service: the service that never bound its listener; the uptime and restart counters are its processes, so the name is the subject rather than a value.

groundTruth.rootCauseReason: The image rebuild pulled the client library's 3.x release, and 2.x had declared `retry` as a top-level option while 3.x declares it inside a `policy` object. The constructor validates what it is given, so the object the service still builds carries a key the library no longer knows, and it throws before the listener binds -- 0.4 seconds after start, not two seconds after a first job, which is the difference between a program that failed to come up and one that came up and then broke. Every attempt fails: the reading that matters is not that it failed but that it failed twenty-four times out of twenty-four, because one failure out of many is an environment and all failures out of all attempts is a deterministic property of the artifact. The ticket states the second half of that argument in its own words -- reproducible in a clean namespace with the same image -- so the case records it as a declared fact rather than re-deriving it, and pair that with the library's major version to make the cause nameable: version three plus a total start failure is a dependency fault, and either one alone is not. Nothing here is a rate that degraded; the service never served at all, which is why the answer is the service even though the repair is a pin in the container's dependency set.

rootCauseIndicators.description: the constructor rejects a key it no longer recognises, which names the incompatibility rather than the symptom
no start succeeds, which separates a deterministic artifact defect from an intermittent environment one
the process lives a fraction of a second, which places the failure before the listener rather than after a first request

causalChain.mechanism: the constructor throws on the retry key within half a second of start, so the container exits before the listener binds and the pod never reaches a ready state
every attempt ends the same way, so the replica count stays at zero for the whole window and the service has nothing to route to

evidenceCheckpoints.description: the major version the rebuilt image resolves to: the ticket says the library went from 2.x to 3.x, and a major number is the whole claim, since an option was moved rather than a patch released
the constructor's refusal names an option it does not know, which is what a moved field looks like from the caller's side and what a wrong credential or a missing host does not
no start succeeds at any point in the window: a share of zero is the deterministic case, where a share between zero and one would leave the artifact and point at the environment
twenty-four attempts in thirty minutes -- about one per backoff interval, so the count also says the kubelet was throttling rather than looping freely
less than a second of life, which is the measurement that puts the failure in construction rather than in handling: a process that comes up and then breaks lives for seconds at least
the ticket's own control: the same image fails in a namespace that shares nothing with production, which is the fact that removes the cluster from the list of explanations

remediation.action: pin the client library to the 2.x line until the retry policy is migrated, so the rebuild cannot silently take a major version
fail the image build when a dependency resolves to a new major version, so the discovery happens in CI rather than at container start

query: The shipping service has not come up once since the image was rebuilt, and the same image fails the same way in a namespace that shares nothing with production. What is the root cause, and why is this not an environment problem?
